page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring AMD EPYC 7571 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with multi-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and features a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance tradeoffs. Single-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng single-core, geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores landing in the middle 50%. The memory subsystem demonstrates strong performance in small-block read-only cached memory bandwidth, ranking in the top 25%, while large-block read and write bandwidths remain average. Cryptographic capabilities are also notable, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 25%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA_NI instructions.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and large local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads that require fast local scratch space. It supports database operations, caching layers, and large-scale data processing. The qualitative cost efficiency of the r5ad.24xlarge is characterized by its high resource density, offering a substantial memory footprint and local NVMe storage on AMD hardware, which typically provides a different cost-to-performance profile compared to Intel-based equivalents. However, the lower single-core CPU performance suggests it is less optimal for single-threaded compute-bound tasks or latency-sensitive sequential processing.
